mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which increases consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of periods following a UNRATE decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates monetary tightening, which may reduce corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >50% of periods following a FEDFUNDS increase above 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) jointly indicates strong demand in the housing and consumer sectors, which drives economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >30% of periods following joint increases in HOUST and RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased supply and economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of periods following an INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >35% of periods following a GDPC1 increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.2% month-over-month signals a strong labor market, which increases consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >45% of periods following a PAYEMS increase >0.2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with an increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates supportive monetary policy for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >30% of periods following a FEDFUNDS decline and GDPC1 increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) during a monetary tightening cycle signals inflationary pressures, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >50% of periods following a CPIAUCSL increase during a tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.
